title: Finite cut-response and intervention-design identifiability seed

object.sets: finite labelled X and Y; hidden H labels are gauge
object.mechanisms: all deterministic maps h:X->H and g:H->Y
object.interventions: do(H=a) for every a in H
object.observed: all g(h(x)) and all g(a), with the hidden intervention interface relabelled by the same gauge
object.gauge_group: Sym(H), acting as h -> pi composed with h and g -> g composed with pi inverse

predeclared_theorem.unrestricted_hidden_use: Compatible gauge orbits are in bijection with a set partition of each environment-output fiber X_y into at most k_y=|g^-1(y)| blocks. Their count is product_y sum_{j=0}^{k_y} S(n_y,j).
predeclared_theorem.surjective_hidden_use: If h is surjective, compatible gauge orbits are in bijection with partitions of X_y into exactly k_y blocks. Their count is product_y S(n_y,k_y).
predeclared_theorem.identifiability_unrestricted: Exactly when every output y has n_y<=1 or k_y<=1.
predeclared_theorem.identifiability_surjective: Exactly when every realized output y has k_y=1 or k_y=n_y.

registered_counterexample.interpretation: All input configurations and all hidden interventions are registered, g and both h maps are surjective, but the two h maps induce different input partitions and are not related by one hidden relabeling.

registered_singleton_do_counterexample.graph: three independent fair Boolean parents X1,X2,X3 -> observed Boolean Y
registered_singleton_do_counterexample.measurements: passive output count and every singleton perfect-intervention output count do(X_i=b); corresponding means are fixed row-scalings but the sealed receipt stores integer counts
registered_singleton_do_counterexample.output_labels: observed Boolean labels 0 and 1 are frozen semantic labels, not gauge
registered_singleton_do_counterexample.expected_result: identical registered integer-count measurements, every parent essential, distinct registered input-gauge orbits, and truth-table difference in the exact design kernel
registered_singleton_do_counterexample.interpretation: Singleton cut coverage sees only the constant and first-order Boolean interaction subspace; higher-order interactions remain unidentified.

gates.G1: zero orbit-count mismatches against the partition formula and exact analytic model/surjection census on every full-grid cell
gates.G2: every one of model_count times |Sym(H)| registered hidden relabelings is enumerated and preserves the observation signature
gates.G3: the registered counterexample has one observation signature and two distinct gauge orbits, with all stated surjectivity checks passing
gates.G4: when |H|=|Y|=2 and g and h are surjective, every observation signature has exactly one compatible gauge orbit
gates.G5: the registered three-parent singleton-do pair has identical measurements, distinct gauge orbits, all parents essential, exact design rank 4 of 8, and difference vector in the design kernel
gates.G6: the executed chain/star fixtures and expected counts exactly match the registered protocol values
gates.G7: the current output path passes non-aliasing and write-once preflight, the runner writes exclusively, and it emits a SHA-256 sidecar
gates.G8: the run records the registration commit and argv, verifies source/protocol/theorem bytes equal their committed blobs before enumeration, and rejects any pre/post hash change

claim_boundary: The mathematical proof establishes the finite-chain counting theorem. A pass exhaustively verifies only the registered bounded grid and implementation, and verifies two exact finite counterexamples to bare cut coverage: downstream state aliasing and singleton-intervention rank deficiency. It does not turn bounded enumeration into a proof of the universal theorem, resolve the generic analytic ASMP-1 conjecture, establish transformer identifiability, or justify a causal abstraction outside the registered finite models.
